708915.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *(s)meyg-, *(s)mēyg- (“small, thin, delicate”), thereby cognate with e.g.

708960.t: From Proto-Indo-European *mneh₂- (“to remind”), which is generally thought to be a root extension of *men- (“to remember, mind”).

708964.t: From μνάομαι (mnáomai, “to be mindful of, remember”) + -μη (-mē).

708939.t: From Proto-Indo-European *misdʰós (“reward; salary”). Cognates include Proto-Indo-Iranian *miždʰám (“reward”), Proto-Germanic *mizdō (“meed”), and Proto-Slavic *mьzdà (“payment, pay”).

708947.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *mewHdʰ- (“to complain, be emotional about”), and compared with Latin maereō (“to mourn”). However, Beekes argues in favor of a Pre-Greek origin, based on the suffix -σος (-sos).

708923.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mneh₂- (“to remind”), which is generally thought to be a root extension of *men- (“to remember, think”), with inchoative suffix -σκω (-skō).

708963.t: From μνήμη (mnḗmē, “memory”) + -εῖον (-eîon), from μνάομαι (mnắomai, “I am mindful of”) + -μη (-mē).

708980.t: Possibly an -ός (-ós) agent noun of ὀμείχω (omeíkhō, “to urinate”), used as a vulgar expression, but this is disputed.

708992.t: Derived from μόνος (mónos, “single, only”) + ἀρχός (arkhós, “ruler, leader”).

708959.t: From Aramaic 𐡌𐡍𐡄 (mnh), from Akkadian 𒈠𒉡𒌑 (manû).

708900.t: According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin, due to the lack of clear cognates.

708950.t: Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *mey- (“to bind”) or a loan from an Indo-Iranian source.

708987.t: Denominative in -ύνω (-ū́nō), like παλύνω (pălū́nō, “to bestrew; to besprinkle”) and φορύνω (phorū́nō, “to be mingled”), from an unattested base form.

708934.t: From *meyḱ-, *meyǵ-. This term perhaps continues Proto-Indo-European *miǵ-sḱéti, itself from the root variant *meyǵ-.

708999.t: From μονο- (mono-) + κέρας (kéras). The long ω results from a contraction of Proto-Hellenic *-kerahos, from the s-stem *kéras plus an o-suffix.
